description: Two instruction working sets: one that fits the frozen 1 KiB I-cache and one four times its capacity. Both bodies are addi on a single register -- no loads, no stores, no branches inside the body -- so what separates the two ROIs is instruction fetch.

roi.name: iws_resident
roi.description: a 32-instruction body, 192 bytes measured, re-entered 2000 times

roi.name: iws_exceeds
roi.description: a 1024-instruction body, 4140 bytes measured, re-entered 64 times

expected_retired_derivation: counted from the disassembly by experiments/IPS-campaign/workloads/check_retirement.py, which also confirms the assembler did not relax the backward jump
baseline_expectation: the baseline core has no instruction cache, so the two ROIs should cost the same PER INSTRUCTION. A difference there would mean the probe is measuring something other than fetch locality.
